payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: pass: The mug is visibly to the right of the headphones. fail: The mug is visibly not to the right of the headphones. unknown: Their relative positions cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image and compare the mug’s position with the headphones; this directly tests the requested outcome.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and criteria appear to collapse two distinct questions: whether the mug is right of the headphones in the edited image, and whether the requested move was completed relative to the source. The edited image shows multiple mug-like objects and a blurred blue remnant on the left, so identity/continuity is ambiguous; the trace’s confident claim that “the mug” is right of the headphones is not enough to establish that the original mug was moved there. Make the decision explicitly use source-to-edit evidence to track the requested mug and assess both progress and completion, while treating ambiguous object identity or uncertain comparison as unresolved rather than inferring completion from a supporting observation. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not proof of a particular mug’s identity or an atomic visual fact. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a semantic binding/evidence and confidence-calibration issue.
s2: The binding is too vague to reliably identify the original mug or distinguish evidence of movement from evidence that the requested edit is complete. Make the node compare source and edited images, track the source mug using visible attributes and position, and judge only whether that same mug has moved relative to the headphones; do not treat any mug-like object on the headphones’ right as proof of continuity or completion. Here the edited image contains multiple mugs and a blurred blue remnant where the source mug was, so the trace’s confident claim that “the mug” is right of the headphones is not well-supported. Keep progress and fulfillment distinct: this support node should report evidence of change, not silently convert a changed relative position into completed fulfillment. If identity or the comparison is genuinely indeterminate, preserve that uncertainty and calibrate confidence to the visual evidence. The aggregate reference label is guidance, not atomic proof. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; address semantic binding, evidence, and confidence calibration.
